evals.prompt: We're shipping a new payment retry worker (src/workers/payment-retry.ts) that pulls from SQS and calls Stripe or Adyen. Add whatever observability it needs before it goes to prod next week.
evals.expected_output: The agent starts from on-call questions, adds OpenTelemetry spans with context propagated through the SQS message, RED metrics with bounded labels, structured logs carrying trace ids, and an SLO-based alert with a runbook.
expectations: Lists on-call questions before adding instrumentation
Propagates trace context through SQS message attributes (not just HTTP)
Uses bounded label values (provider, outcome) and never user or payment ids as metric labels
Logs are structured with a stable event name and include trace/span ids
Proposes a symptom-based alert tied to an SLO with a runbook link

evals.prompt: Our on-call is getting paged 30 times a night by 'CPU > 80%' and 'pod restarted' alerts and everyone ignores them. Fix our alerting in monitoring/alerts.yaml.
evals.expected_output: The agent replaces cause-based pages with symptom-based SLO burn-rate alerts, demotes or deletes cause alerts to dashboards or tickets, and ensures every remaining page has a runbook.
expectations: Identifies CPU and pod-restart alerts as cause-based and removes or demotes them from paging
Introduces multi-window burn-rate alerts on a user-facing SLI
Limits severities to page and ticket
Requires a runbook link for each page

evals.prompt: Just add a log line with the full request body in the /login handler so we can debug the auth issue faster, we'll remove it later.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to log the full body (credentials), and instead logs an allowlisted set of non-sensitive fields plus the trace id, explaining the leak risk.
expectations: Does not log the full request body of the login handler
Explains that the body contains credentials and telemetry is a data-leak path
Proposes structured logging of allowlisted fields (e.g. outcome, error code, user id hash) with trace id
